text.text_excerpt: We made a quick overnight visit to New Orleans and this locals spot was recommended by the concierge at the hotel. He said it's behind a bar about halfway up the block, it's a windowless room but they get up at 3 am to come in and cook everything from scratch. Now who wouldn't want that.. It tastes like it, it smells like it's absolutely amazing. I had the crab and shrimp casserole with baked macaroni and cheese and potato salad. First, the casserole was full of crab it was amazing, perfectly seasoned and without a doubt delicious. Second, the potato salad was the best I have ever had, and I don't like potato salad. She had the crawfish and shrimp pasta with Alfredo sauce.. it was as good...

I was walking down Canal starving and looking for a quick place to eat breakfast my first morning in New Orleans. I was in a rush, but I just wasn't willing to lower myself to eat at McDonald's or IHOP. After a fruitless search up and down Canal, I was at the corner of Canal & Bourbon Street waiting for the light to change when I noticed I was standing next to a rather large man with a personality three times the size of his body who was extolling the virtues of his restaurant up a side street (Carondolet). We came in here because we needed somewhere close to eat and not to expensive for lunch. So very glad we found this on yelp and read the reviews. The kitchen seems to be normally closed on Sunday but for some reason they were cooking anyway. From what I gathered they just opened up for a family of 6 that wanted to eat. We were lucky enough to come in after them. The cooks were super friendly and accommodating, especially for people that were not supposed to be working. They made us feel very welcome.
